answer: Each agent identity must lock a stake in a shared vault, sized by measured lifetime output rather than declared reputation. A new key can claim output only by walking a long warm-up vine of settled tasks attested by peers who also stake on it. Cloning a history onto many keys fails because every duplicate needs its own independent stake and its own warm-up work, so attacker cost scales linearly with identities, while slashing makes spam unprofitable. A Sybil cluster then behaves like a glacier: it moves only slowly, at steady expense.
